# #403 — SHAPE-3: What is the OB-native kind vocabulary, and does 'correction' ever expire?

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: question, memory

Updated: 2026-07-25T03:30:03Z

---

Parent: #400. **Question, not work. Do not implement.** Feeds R1.

## Context

`docs/code-brain-design.md` §1 R1 needs three axes; only `scope` exists today:

| Axis | Question | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **kind** | how fast does it go stale | missing |
| **reach** | project-only, or applies everywhere | `shared-kb` exists, nothing routes to it |
| scope | who owns it | namespace / lane |

Borrowed shape from gbrain `src/core/facts/decay.ts` — per-kind half-lives,
chosen empirically in a documented review (`event` 7d, `commitment` 90d,
`preference` 90d, `belief` 365d, `fact` 365d). **Their kinds are
personal-assistant kinds and must not be copied.**

Candidate OB-native kinds, from the doc:

| Kind | Example | Lean |
|---|---|---|
| `decision` | "0.91 dedupe, per the LiteLLM rule" | long |
| `correction` | "recency does not win supersession" | **longest — arguably never** |
| `state` | "wheel is 0.1.17", "maintenance is off" | short, 7-14d |
| `outcome` | "PR #378 merged, CI green" | short, historically permanent |
| `pattern` | "agents drift when left autonomous" | long, and dangerous |

## The three open questions

**1. Is that the right list?** It was written in one pass. `state` and `outcome`
in particular may be the same kind at different times — "maintenance is off" is a
state; "maintenance was turned on in PR #384" is an outcome; a week later the
outcome *is* the state.

**2. Does `correction` ever expire?** The doc says *"longest — arguably never"*
and gives the reason: **every real fix in that session was Rico correcting the
agent.** Those are the highest-value rows in the system. But never-expiring is a
strong claim — a correction to a design that got deleted is a correction to
nothing. Candidate resolution: corrections do not expire on a **clock**, they
expire when their **subject** does, which makes it a link problem rather than a
half-life problem.

**3. Which kinds are `pattern`, and why is `pattern` dangerous?** The doc flags
it without expanding. Best reading: a `pattern` is an inference *about* other
rows, so it can be reinforced by the very drift it should be detecting — "agents
drift when left autonomous" gets stronger every time drift happens, and never
gets weaker when it does not. A kind that only accumulates is a kind that
eventually wins every ranking.

## Why half-lives cannot be guessed

gbrain's are documented as chosen empirically in a review, with stated reasons
(*"lunch on Tuesday is meaningless after Tuesday"*). Copying numbers without the
reasoning gets the numbers *and* loses the ability to defend them. OB has no
equivalent measurement yet.

## What would settle it

Take ~50 real rows from `thoughts` / `decisions`, hand-label them with the
candidate kinds, and count: which rows do not fit any kind, and which kinds catch
only one row? A kind vocabulary that cannot classify its own corpus is wrong.

**Do not set half-life numbers until that count exists.** The `kind` column can
land first; the numbers are a separate decision with a separate evidence bar.

## Related

Reinforcement is a **separate axis** from confidence — gbrain salience is
`emotional_weight * 5 + ln(1 + take_count)`, log-damped so the 50th mention
counts less than the 2nd. See #398 and the standing-hazard table in
`docs/code-brain-design.md` (the naive "+0.2 to confidence" proposal was wrong).
